body.html: GRAND PA Hotel & Resort sits at 110/1 Lamphun-Doi Ti Road in the Wiang Yong area of Mueang Lamphun, on the eastern side of the Kuang River · It's just outside the old town but very convenient, as it's only about 1 minute by car from Chaem Fa Shopping Mall and Major Cineplex and around 5 minutes from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai · Driving into Chiang Mai city takes about 40 minutes, and Chiang Mai Airport is around 32 km away · It suits self-drivers who want a well-equipped stay with easy parking.

The property is a newly opened hotel split into a hotel building with 83 rooms and a resort building with 42 rooms (including VIP rooms), 125 in total · The standout feature of the rooms is that they're spacious and clean, with comfortable beds and mattresses, air-conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen TV, a work desk, free Wi-Fi and a separated wet-and-dry bathroom · There's a range of types from Premium Deluxe and Deluxe to Junior Suite and Penthouse Suite · Real guest reviews very often praise the room size and cleanliness, especially against a rate in the low-thousand-baht range.

"Really big, clean rooms with comfy mattresses, a large pool and a good gym. The breakfast exceeded expectations — better than many hotels I've stayed at. Friendly staff, and handy being next to Chaem Fa mall."

What sets GRAND PA apart from the usual small boutiques in Lamphun is its full resort-style facilities · There's a large outdoor pool with a pool bar, a gym that several reviews call well-equipped, the Wiang Yong cafe and restaurant, a fresh on-site bakery, a mini-mart, and meeting rooms for 20 to 400 people that suit seminars or functions · For a small town like Lamphun, having a big pool and a gym in one place is not something you find often.

Breakfast is the most talked-about part in reviews · Many guests say the buffet breakfast here exceeds expectations, with plenty of choice and a taste better than hotels charging more, served around 7:00–10:00 · One thing to know is that the menu leans Asian/Thai rather than Western, so anyone after a full continental spread may find the Western options thinner · Service overall earns praise for friendly, attentive staff.

On scores, GRAND PA performs consistently well · Trip.com rates it around 8.8 from 141 reviews, while Tripadvisor/Google sit around 4.4 out of 5, with repeated praise for big rooms, cleanliness, the pool and the breakfast · For a newly opened hotel still building its review base, that's a solid set of numbers and reflects a 4-star stay that's good value in Lamphun.

A few things to know before booking · First, the location is outside the old town — if you want to stroll the walking street or visit old-town temples in the evening, you'll need to drive or grab a ride; it's not a walk-to-everything stay · Second, the building is close to a main road, and some reviews note road noise at night in rooms facing the street, so light sleepers should ask for an interior room · And the room decor is simple with white walls — functional but not flashy, so anyone expecting bold design may find it plain.

In short, GRAND PA Hotel & Resort suits travellers after a hotel-resort with big rooms, a large pool, a gym and a good breakfast in the low-to-mid thousand-baht range in Lamphun · It's a strong pick for families, self-drivers, or groups coming for meetings and functions · But if you want to stay within the old town and walk to the temples, or want a design-led boutique in the heart of the city, it's worth comparing old-town options too.

honestSummary: GRAND PA Hotel & Resort is a newly opened 4-star boutique hotel-resort in the Wiang Yong area of Lamphun that delivers big rooms, a large pool, a gym and a good breakfast in the low-to-mid thousand-baht range, with a location next to Chaem Fa Mall and free parking — ideal for families, self-drivers and groups coming for meetings · Just accept that it's outside the old town, you can't walk to the temples, and street-facing rooms can get some road noise.
honestChecks: If you want to stay within the old town and walk to Wat Phra That — this place is on the Wiang Yong side, outside the old town, so you'll need to drive or grab a ride → if walking the old town in the evening matters, compare old-town options too.

If you're a light sleeper — the building is near a main road and some reviews note night-time road noise in street-facing rooms → ask for an interior or higher-floor room at booking, and pack earplugs just in case.
If you like a full continental breakfast — the buffet here is good but leans Asian/Thai, with fewer Western options → set expectations, or head into town for a cafe to top up.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — GRAND PA Hotel & Resort Lamphun

faq.q: Where is GRAND PA Hotel & Resort and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 110/1 Lamphun-Doi Ti Road in the Wiang Yong area of Mueang Lamphun · It's only about 1 minute by car from Chaem Fa Shopping Mall and Major Cineplex · About 5 minutes from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and around 7 minutes from the old town centre · Driving into Chiang Mai city takes about 40 minutes, and Chiang Mai Airport is around 32 km away.

faq.q: How much does GRAND PA Hotel & Resort cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx ฿1,050/night for a Premium Deluxe room · The range runs from Deluxe and Junior Suite up to a Penthouse Suite · All rooms are spacious with air-conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen TV and free Wi-Fi · Prices shift with season and festivals, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does it have a swimming pool and gym?
faq.a: Yes — there's a large outdoor pool with a pool bar and a gym, which is not common in Lamphun · There's also the Wiang Yong cafe and restaurant, a fresh on-site bakery, a mini-mart and meeting rooms for 20–400 people.

faq.q: What's the breakfast like at GRAND PA?
faq.a: Breakfast is a buffet that many reviews say exceeds expectations, with plenty of choice, served around 7:00–10:00 · The menu leans Asian/Thai, so anyone after a full continental breakfast may find the Western options thinner.

faq.q: Who is GRAND PA Hotel & Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a strong pick for families, self-drivers, or groups coming for meetings and functions who want a hotel-resort with big rooms, a pool, a gym and a good breakfast in the low-to-mid thousand-baht range · It's less ideal for those who want to stay within the old town and walk to the temples, or want a design-led boutique in the heart of the city.

faq.q: Are the rooms noisy, and is it far from Chiang Mai city?
faq.a: The building is near a main road · Some reviews note road noise at night in street-facing rooms, so light sleepers should ask for an interior or higher-floor room · On distance, it's in Lamphun town and about a 40-minute drive into Chiang Mai city, so it works best as a base for both towns rather than purely for visiting Chiang Mai.
